docs.title: PYTA Backend
docs.text: PYTA is a FastAPI-based backend focused on secure authentication and encrypted credential storage.

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text:
• Email + password authentication
  • Secure password hashing
  • Session-based authentication
  • PostgreSQL database
  • SQLModel ORM
  • Cookie-based sessions

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text:
• FastAPI
  • SQLModel + SQLAlchemy
  • PostgreSQL
  • Passlib
  • Pydantic Settings

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: PYTA follows a modular backend architecture.

docs.title: Core Modules
docs.text: Module Responsibility auth_router.py Authentication endpoints models.py Database models db.py Database engine & sessions passwords.py Password hashing settings.py Environment configuration

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text:
1. Client sends request
  2. FastAPI route handles logic
  3. Database session is injected
  4. SQLModel performs queries
  5. Response returned with cookie/session

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Authentication is session-based using cookies.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. User logs in or registers
  2. Password is hashed with PBKDF2
  3. Session record is created
  4. Session ID is stored in an HTTP-only cookie

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
• session_id
  • HTTP-only
  • Secure in production
  • SameSite=Lax

docs.title: Session handling
docs.text:
• Sessions are stored in the database
  • Session ID is sent as an HTTP-only cookie
  • Cookies are marked secure in non-debug mode

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration is handled using pydantic-settings.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default DB_HOST Database host localhost POSTGRES_PORT DB port 5432 POSTGRES_USER DB user postgres POSTGRES_PASSWORD DB password example POSTGRES_DB DB name postgres SEED_DB Seed database false

docs.title: Example .env
docs.text: ```env DB_HOST=localhost POSTGRES_USER=postgres POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret POSTGRES_DB=pyta DEBUG=true

docs.title: Database
docs.text: PYTA uses PostgreSQL with SQLModel.

docs.title: Engine creation
docs.text:
• Connection URLs are constructed safely using URL encoding
  • Engines are cached using LRU caching
  • Connection health is ensured with pool_pre_ping

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Stores login credentials.

  • email (unique)
  • password (hashed)
  • role_id

docs.title: User
docs.text:
Stores encryption keys and links to auth.

  • encryption_key (binary)
  • one-to-one with Auth

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
Represents a login session.

  • HTTP-only cookie based
  • Stored server-side

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Encrypted credential storage.

  • username_data
  • password_data
  • domains
  • notes

docs.title: Implemented protections
docs.text:
• Password hashing (PBKDF2)
  • HTTP-only cookies
  • Encrypted storage fields
  • Server-side sessions
  • Environment-based secrets

docs.title: Authentication API (/auth)
docs.text:
All authentication endpoints are grouped under the /auth prefix.

Authentication is session-based and uses HTTP-only cookies to store the session identifier.

docs.title: POST /auth/register
docs.text: Register a new user account and immediately create a session.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Body

{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "strongpassword"
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Status: 201 Created

Body

{
  "session_id": "uuid"
}

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Fails if the email is already registered
  • Hashes the password before storing it

  • Creates:

  • Auth record

  • User record
  • Session record
  • Sets an HTTP-only cookie named session_id

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Reason 409 Email already registered

docs.title: POST /auth/login
docs.text: Authenticate an existing user and create a new session.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Body

{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "strongpassword"
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Status: 200 OK

Body

{
  "session_id": "uuid"
}

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Verifies password using PBKDF2 hash comparison
  • Creates a new session in the database
  • Sets an HTTP-only cookie named session_id

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Reason 401 Invalid email or password 500 User record missing in database

docs.title: POST /auth/logout
docs.text: Log out the current session.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
No request body is required.

The session ID is read from one of the following:

  • session_id cookie
  • X-Session-Id header

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Status: 204 No Content

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Deletes the session from the database if it exists
  • Always clears the session_id cookie
  • Safe to call even if no session is active

docs.title: Session Cookies
docs.text:
All authentication endpoints that create a session set a cookie with the following properties:

Attribute Value Name session_id HTTP Only true Secure true (disabled in debug mode) SameSite lax

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Sessions are server-side, not JWT-based
  • Multiple concurrent sessions per user are allowed
  • Session lifetime is controlled by database cleanup logic

docs.title: Sync API (/sync)
docs.text:
All sync endpoints are grouped under the /sync prefix.

Sync is used to synchronize encrypted credential storage between the client and server.

docs.title: GET /sync/changes
docs.text: Retrieve changes from the server since a specific cursor or timestamp.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Query Parameters

  • cursor (optional): Resume from a specific point
  • since (optional): ISO timestamp to fetch changes after

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Status: 200 OK

Body

{
  "changes": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "username_data": "bytes",
      "password_data": "bytes",
      "domains": ["bytes"],
      "notes": "bytes",
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00",
      "updated": "2026-01-01T00:00:00",
      "deleted_at": null
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "string",
  "has_more": false
}

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Returns all storage changes since the given cursor or timestamp
  • Includes created, updated, and deleted items
  • Supports pagination via cursor
  • Requires authentication (session cookie)

docs.title: POST /sync/push
docs.text: Push local changes to the server (creates, updates, deletes).

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Body

{
  "creates": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "username_data": "bytes",
      "password_data": "bytes",
      "domains": ["bytes"],
      "notes": "bytes",
      "updated": "2026-01-01T00:00:00"
    }
  ],
  "updates": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "username_data": "bytes",
      "password_data": "bytes",
      "domains": ["bytes"],
      "notes": "bytes",
      "updated": "2026-01-01T00:00:00"
    }
  ],
  "deletes": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "updated": "2026-01-01T00:00:00"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Status: 200 OK

Body

{
  "success_count": 5,
  "conflict_count": 1,
  "conflicts": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "reason": "server_updated_after_client"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Processes creates, updates, and deletes in a single request
  • Detects conflicts using timestamps
  • Returns conflict information for client resolution
  • All data is encrypted client-side before transmission
  • Requires authentication (session cookie)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Reason 401 Not authenticated 409 Conflict (see conflicts)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• All credential data is encrypted on the client before sync
  • The server stores only encrypted blobs
  • Conflicts are resolved by timestamp comparison
  • Multiple devices can sync to the same account
